text:
Recent work supports modeling elapsed time alongside sequence position. [TemProxRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784) combines absolute and relative temporal/positional embeddings in self-attention, plus temporal-proximity contrastive learning. [TLSTSRec (online 2024; volume 2025)](https://doi.org/10.3233/IDA-240051) explores time-aware long/short-term preference modeling. The earlier [TiSASRec](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/wsdm20b.pdf) provides the foundational mechanism: pairwise time-interval embeddings alongside position information. These are transferable temporal mechanisms, not evidence that replacing the BERT4Rec backbone is necessary.

A [2026 BERT4Rec session-enhancement paper](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44163-026-01554-z) combines content relevance with continuous temporal decay and learned long/short-term gating. It reports improvements over vanilla BERT4Rec and simple decay, but its deployment pipeline and additional attributes differ from this benchmark; reported gains do not establish RecHarness performance. Its useful hypothesis is adaptive retention of older relevant interactions rather than unconditional recency weighting.

Suggested experiment, inferred from these mechanisms: retain one jointly trained BERT4Rec per category; add head-specific learned log-bucket time-gap biases to bidirectional attention, optionally with a nonnegative learned decay coefficient. Compare against the established sampling control under the same validation protocol. Preserve masked-target training and appended-mask inference; derive temporal features solely from available history timestamps. The appended mask must use a documented history-only time reference, never the held-out interaction timestamp. Read out the final nonpadding mask position and preserve predictor/checkpoint consistency.
